design: Post hoc sensitivity of an already known retrospective result; not preregistration or independent validation
question: Does earlier-screen-only guide selection retain a later-screen depletion shift when the older selection score excludes the evaluated cell context?
input: Frozen Table S25; all 1251 guide-cell rows in the existing 87-product, 417-guide selection cohort
rule: For each product and evaluation cell, average older LFC over the other two cells, select the two lowest-scoring guides, resolve ties by lexicographic guide sequence, and evaluate only the later LFC in the excluded cell
reference: Exact expectation under uniform random selection of two eligible guides without replacement, equal to the all-eligible-guide mean for that product and evaluation cell
outputs: All product-cell selected guides, later scores and selected-minus-reference contrasts
Equal-product mean shift in each of the three held-out contexts
Descriptive median and count of negative/zero/positive product-average shifts for the original and held-out-context strategies
All single-product omissions for the held-out-context mean
uncertainty: 2000 dependence-group bootstrap samples with NumPy default_rng seed 20261026, retaining all cells jointly; nominal 95 percent percentile intervals for descriptive post hoc sensitivity, no new confirmatory hypothesis test
no_tuning: No alternate cohort, guide minimum, selection count, cell subset or score is chosen based on results
verification: Reproduce original v18 selection estimate and per-cell values; independently reconstruct selections from a guide-by-cell matrix; verify exact random-pair expectation by enumerating all pairs for every product-cell
interpretation_limits: The three fixed cell contexts and products were already known and are not new validation samples
The evaluated cell is excluded only from the older selection score; this is not evaluation in a biologically unseen cell line
Different evaluated cells may select different guide pairs
Nominal intervals condition on retrospective analysis choices and are not multiplicity-adjusted across the research program
No molecular mechanism, false-positive target, clinical utility or optimal guide strategy is established
